statement: Zarii is committed to 100% free, high-quality, open-access education. Our dictionary and lexical engines are built strictly upon open-source and permissively licensed linguistic corpora.

sources.name: Open English WordNet (2024 Edition)
sources.description: Comprehensive English lexical database providing synsets, definitions, semantic domains, relations, examples, and morphological exception indexes.
sources.attributionText: Open English WordNet 2024 by the Global WordNet Association, based on Princeton University WordNet 3.0. Licensed under CC BY 4.0.

sources.name: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary
sources.description: North American English pronunciation dictionary with over 134,000 phonetic transcriptions, mapped to International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) and readable respelling.
sources.attributionText: The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, Copyright (C) 1993-2015 Carnegie Mellon University. Free for commercial and educational use with attribution.

sources.name: Google Web Trillion Word N-Grams & OpenSubtitles Frequency
sources.organization: Google Inc., Peter Norvig & Hermit Dave
sources.description: Statistical word frequency lists used to compute CEFR level estimates (A1 to C1) and sort definitions by real-world usage prevalence.
sources.attributionText: Frequency rankings computed using datasets by Peter Norvig (Google Web Trillion Word Corpus) and Hermit Dave (OpenSubtitles).

sources.name: DWYL English Words
sources.description: Open English headword spell-checking list used solely for lexical validation (no definitions or proprietary texts).
sources.attributionText: Spelling validation aided by dwyl english-words (Public Domain).

exclusions: No copyrighted material from Oxford, Cambridge, Longman, Merriam-Webster, or other proprietary dictionaries is utilized.
